picks.title: OpenAI’s chief scientist has thoughts on how to limit AI development
picks.post: Before anyone sets a speed limit on AI development, someone has to agree on how to measure speed. Good luck with that one.
picks.reason: OpenAI's chief scientist on AI pacing, a sharp framing of the regulation debate.
picks.card_text: Speed limit needs an agreed measure of speed

picks.title: Europe's STOXX 600 rises as tech shares rebound after AI-driven rout
picks.post: Tech shares bounced back after an AI-driven rout, which is the market's way of saying it has already forgotten last week. Give it a few days.
picks.reason: Market-level signal on AI stock sentiment after a sharp selloff.
picks.card_text: Tech shares rebound after AI-driven rout

picks.title: How Notable Capital, GIC, and Baillie Gifford bet big on Anthropic before its IPO
picks.post: Notable Capital, GIC and Baillie Gifford explain why they bet billions on Anthropic before its IPO. Conviction is cheap to describe in hindsight; the IPO price will do the grading.
picks.reason: Pre-IPO backers of Anthropic detailing big bets, relevant to frontier AI valuations.
picks.card_text: Backers bet billions before Anthropic's IPO

picks.title: Insight: How Nvidia’s billion-dollar turnaround in China is threatened by Huang’s exit
picks.post: Nvidia's billion-dollar China turnaround is now threatened by Jensen Huang's exit. So the comeback depended on one person's calendar. Curious how much of it survives without him.
picks.reason: Nvidia China revenue recovery at risk from leadership change; directly relevant to the chip market.
picks.card_text: Billion-dollar China turnaround, now at risk

picks.title: The Enigma of SoftBank’s $1 Trillion SK Hynix Buyout Attempt
picks.post: SoftBank floated a $1 trillion buyout of SK Hynix, which EE Times says was a non-starter from the start. Still, it shows how badly everyone wants memory capacity for the AI buildout.
picks.reason: Shows strategic value of memory chipmakers in the AI buildout, even for a deal that never had a chance.

picks.title: Consortium in talks to buy LCY's $600 million China chip chemicals business, people say
picks.post: A consortium is reportedly in talks for LCY's $600 million China chip chemicals business. Everyone wants a piece of the chip supply chain, just not the parts that make the headlines.
picks.reason: Chip materials M&A in China; a supply-chain signal, though a smaller story.

picks.title: Over half of all console players active on GTA 6's launch day played it, says Circana
picks.post: Circana says more than half of everyone playing on PS5 and Xbox on GTA 6's launch day was playing GTA 6. Impressive reach, though nobody has measured how many of those players were just ignoring the rest of their library.
picks.reason: Concrete platform-wide engagement figure from a credible market tracker.
picks.card_text: More than half of console players, launch day

picks.title: Unreal Engine 6 to jettison key scripting feature earlier than planned in favor of AI coding
picks.post: Unreal Engine 6 will drop Blueprints earlier than planned in favor of AI coding. Visual scripting existed so people didn't have to write code, so retiring it for a tool that writes code is an interesting choice.
picks.reason: Major engine platform shift toward AI-assisted development, affecting many studios.
picks.card_text: Blueprints cut early for AI coding

picks.title: Activision patents AI voice system that learns from in-game chat and creates audio for NPCs who can even speak in place of you
picks.post: Activision has patented a system that listens to player voice chat after key moments and recreates it for NPCs, who can speak in place of you. Turning players' trash talk into training data is a bold move from a company that still needs everyone to log in.
picks.reason: Notable AI-in-games patent tying voice chat to NPC generation; signals publisher direction.
picks.card_text: Patent: NPCs trained on player voice chat

picks.title: VC funding rebounds as startups raise $255M; Women founders driving social change
picks.post: 22 new-age tech companies made their public market debut in FY26. That's a lot of listings to justify in one year, and I'm curious how many are still trading above their issue price.
picks.reason: Concrete count of new-age tech IPOs in FY26, a clear signal for the Indian listings market.
picks.card_text: 22 new-age tech companies listed in FY26

picks.title: Sarvam clarifies AI strategy amid debate over hosting Chinese models
picks.post: Sarvam says a model's country of origin and where it runs are "two different matters." For a company pitching homegrown AI, the hosting bill is the part people will read closely.
picks.reason: Sarvam's defence of hosting Chinese models touches on sovereignty and the credibility of India's AI push.
picks.card_text: Origin and hosting are "two different matters"

picks.title: India may emerge as long-term AI winner despite dependence on foreign tech: Deutsche Bank
picks.post: Deutsche Bank says India could be one of the biggest long-term AI winners, citing population, digital infrastructure and talent. Long-term winner is a comfortable phrase for a report; the open question is who captures the value.
picks.reason: Broker view on India's AI economic upside, useful context on whether the thesis holds.
picks.card_text: One of the biggest long-term AI beneficiaries

picks.title: Capita shares plunge 70% as boss quits after civil service pensions failure
picks.post: Capita shares are down 70% after the boss quit over delayed civil service pension payments. Outsourcing a pension scheme was supposed to move the risk off the government, but the people still waiting for their money seem to be carrying it.
picks.reason: A 70% share collapse tied to a specific operational failure. Shows outsourcing risk landing on the public.

picks.title: Catering giant to switch main share listing to US in further blow to UK
picks.post: Another UK company is moving its main listing to the US, with a catering giant the latest to decide London isn't worth the trouble. Which household name gets to turn off the lights next?
picks.reason: Part of a sustained UK listing exodus, a real structural shift in capital markets.
picks.card_text: Main share listing moving to US

picks.title: Poundland is facing collapse - what's gone wrong?
picks.post: Poundland has days to find a buyer or collapse into administration. A chain built on cheap prices running out of buyers is a strange sign for a cost-of-living story.
picks.reason: Concrete distress signal for UK retail and consumer spending, with a days-long deadline.
picks.card_text: Days left to find a buyer

picks.title: GTA 6 Has Already Sold 45 Million Copies, Says Research Firm
picks.post:
A research firm claims GTA 6 has sold nearly 45 million copies in its launch weekend, worth over $4 billion.

The number comes from the research firm, not the publisher.
picks.reason: Huge number everyone can compare to their own spending; the source question invites debate.

picks.title: Metacritic's user review problem worsens, as GTA 6's launch prompts review-bombing for completely unrelated games like Soul Calibur and The Ocarina of Time
picks.post:
GTA 6's Metacritic user scores are being review-bombed, and classic games like Soul Calibur and The Ocarina of Time are getting hit too.

Eurogamer says the fight is now reaching games with no link to GTA 6 at all.
picks.reason: Fan war over user scores hitting beloved unrelated classics; people will pick sides fast.

picks.title: Binding of Isaac DLC adds AI music in GTA 6-parodying update despite not having an AI disclosure, Steam reviews drop to Overwhelmingly Negative, music gets pulled
picks.post:
Nicalis has pulled undisclosed AI-generated music from The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ after a GTA 6 parody update went out.

Steam reviews have dropped to Overwhelmingly Negative.
picks.reason: AI music without disclosure, a backlash that tanked Steam reviews, and a publisher reversing course.

picks.title: Nvidia reverses course and brings Jensen Huang back as CEO
picks.post:
Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, effective immediately, after its board voted unanimously to bring him back.

The share price jumped more than 30%, and senior US government officials reportedly backed the reversal.
picks.reason: Huge name, dramatic U-turn, a 30% stock jump, and a government angle people will argue about.

picks.title: Virginia, Oregon sue Musk's SpaceX over Grok AI's creation of child sexual abuse images and videos
picks.post:
Virginia and Oregon are suing Elon Musk's SpaceX over child sexual abuse images and videos created by its Grok AI.

The states' attorneys general argue sexual images from the chatbot harmed consumers.
picks.reason: Musk, AI-generated child abuse content, and a state lawsuit; people will split on blame and on Grok.

picks.title: Uber now lets you book rides that record the drive by default
picks.post:
Uber is testing rides that record the entire trip by default, using the driver's front phone camera.

The option shows up as "Recorded Rides" in the app, and is being piloted in the US.
picks.reason: Default in-car recording raises privacy questions for both riders and drivers, a feeling everyone has.

picks.title: Pip assessments need 'fundamental overhaul', report to say
picks.post:
Poundland has days to find a buyer or collapse into administration.

A chain built on cheap prices is running out of time, and shoppers and staff are left wondering what happens next.
picks.reason: Household UK name facing a sudden collapse, with jobs and everyday prices at stake.
picks.card_text: Days to find a buyer or collapse

picks.title: Dutch privacy authority urges consumers not to buy ‘pervert glasses’
picks.post:
The Netherlands' data protection agency is urging consumers not to buy smart glasses, which it calls "pervert glasses" in its warning.

It says the wearables violate people's privacy, get information wrong and can lead to unsafe situations.
picks.reason: Privacy fears about camera glasses hit everyday people, and the 'pervert glasses' label invites debate.

picks.title: Microsoft explains the Outlook outage that hit millions
picks.post:
Microsoft says a months-old bug and a chain of cascading failures brought Outlook and other services down worldwide.

The outage hit millions, and Microsoft warns scammers are already using it to convince people their emails are lost.
picks.reason: Huge outage affecting millions plus a scam angle people will share and argue about.

picks.title: Drone attack on Colombian police base injures civilians and damages homes
picks.post:
Meta has dropped its 2030 net zero goal in its 2026 sustainability report.

The decision could send ripples across the tech industry, and it lands as climate pledges become a point of debate.
picks.reason: A big-name company abandoning a climate promise is a clear trust and hypocrisy argument.

picks.title: Xbox Has Looked Into Eliminating Paid Multiplayer – Report
picks.post:
According to a new report, Xbox looked into eliminating paid multiplayer as part of its Xbox Helix strategy.

The report says the idea was considered, not that it was decided.
picks.reason: Taking away a paid feature players already pay for is a classic fan-versus-company flashpoint.

picks.title: Call of Duty's Player Count Dropped by Over 40% Following GTA 6's Release, According to Analysts
picks.post:
A new analyst report says Call of Duty's player count fell by over 40% after GTA 6 launched.

The report ties the drop to GTA 6's release, which came out just days earlier.
picks.reason: Big franchise, big percentage, and a direct rivalry with GTA 6 that fans will argue over.

picks.title: Resident Evil creator Shinji Mikami says he wishes AI would disappear entirely, but that he experiments with it as a tool
picks.post:
Resident Evil creator Shinji Mikami says he wishes AI would disappear entirely, fearing mass job losses.

He still experiments with AI as a tool, and Stellar Blade's CEO shared a G-CON 2026 panel with opposing views.
picks.reason: A famous developer taking a bold stance on AI and jobs, with a public rival view.

picks.title: EXCLUSIVE: Some US banks tighten AI-agent controls on concern about models escaping safeguards
picks.post:
Some US banks are tightening controls on AI agents, software that acts on its own for users, Reuters reports.

The concern is that AI models could escape their safeguards.
picks.reason: Fear of AI escaping safeguards, tied to banks and customers' money, is an easy topic to take sides on.

picks.title: US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal
picks.post:
The US plans to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed over accusations it funneled AI chips to China.

The scandal began when a former Megaspeed executive's affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang became public.
picks.reason: Huang's affair scandal plus alleged chip smuggling to China gives a clear villain and a famous name.
picks.card_text: Accused of funneling AI chips to China

picks.title: Figma employee sues, alleging company forced her to confront harassers
picks.post:
Figma and its CEO are being sued by a current employee over alleged sexual harassment and discrimination.

She says the company forced her to confront the people harassing her.
picks.reason: Well-known app company and CEO accused of workplace harassment; people will pick sides on the company's response.

picks.title: More than 39 million people have played GTA 6 on PlayStation alone, Sony says, as the game breaks all-time player numbers on the platform
picks.post:
Sony says more than 39 million unique people have played GTA 6 on PlayStation alone.

That's more than the 32.5 million day-one sales Take-Two reported across all platforms.
picks.reason: A huge, specific number on GTA 6 that invites a fight over what player counts actually measure versus sales.

picks.title: Cyberleek releases executable for GTA 6 Xbox build leaked last week: 'The torch passes to the open source recomp and emulation projects'
picks.post:
Leaker CyberLeek has released the executable for a near-full GTA 6 Xbox build that leaked last week.

There is still no official PC version, and the torch has now passed to open source emulation projects.
picks.reason: Leak-versus-publisher tension on the most-hyped game, with fans split on piracy and an unannounced PC release.

picks.title: World stocks are mixed after Wall Street's rebound as Jensen Huang returns as Nvidia’s CEO
picks.post:
SpaceX and Tesla have appointed five directors to guide merger talks, the FT reports.

Both companies are run by Elon Musk, and no deal has been announced.
picks.reason: Musk running both sides of a possible merger invites strong opinions on fairness to shareholders.

picks.title: Big Tech could face billions of dollars in fines under Australian internet safety bill
picks.post:
Big Tech could face fines in the billions under an Australian internet safety bill.

The size of the penalties is the number that will split people over how far online platforms should be policed.
picks.reason: Billion-dollar fines on Big Tech for online safety draw strong views from users and critics.
picks.card_text: Fines could reach billions of dollars
